analysis: This PR changes documentation only. In docs/developer/test.md it bumps the date at line 3 and adds lines 173-181 naming GLM5Next test selectors: returnedAssistantReasoningRendersLikeReasoningContent, openRouterReasoningContentReturnRequestIsServed, capturedOpenRouterToolRequestIsServed and capturedOpenRouterToolServesAFiveStepConversation. These describe OpenRouter returned-reasoning replay and captured strict weather-tool requests, with tool choice omitted, auto and none, plus a five-step conversation. Those fixtures are described as held byte for byte and hash-checked. In docs/provider/cli-reference.md it bumps the date and adds "constant or variable frame rate" to the description of video_url input, which is sampled at 2 FPS and decoded target-only. No source, wire protocol, crypto, attestation, authorization, cache-storage or key-handling code changes. No threat-model asset, boundary, assumption or mitigation (T-041, TB-002, TB-007, A-001) is altered or invalidated. The claims about test coverage and variable-frame-rate video support refer to code outside the supplied evidence (decoder and GLM5Next tests), so I could not verify they match the implementation. That is a documentation-accuracy question, not a security regression. The remaining test.md sections (units 6 and 7) are unchanged context, and I found nothing in them that exposes secrets or changes security posture. Integration only needs to confirm that the variable-frame-rate decode path has bounded frame, token and byte limits as the surrounding docs claim. That would be a separate code change and is not in this PR.
